name: Batel
tagline: Curitiba's upmarket strip of towers, restaurants and rooftop bars
description: A dense band of glass residential towers along Avenida do Batel, with the city's best restaurants, wine bars and two shopping centres at street level. Well-off professionals and young couples live here. It is the most comfortable area to walk at night and the default choice for visitors with a budget.
bestFor: Remote workers who want restaurants, gyms and coworking within a few blocks and will pay for it.
pros: Best restaurant and cafe density in the city
Modern towers with gyms, coworking rooms and fibre
cons: The most expensive rents in Curitiba
Avenue traffic noise on lower floors

name: Centro
tagline: Pedestrian streets, historic blocks and every bus line
description: The historic core, where Rua XV de Novembro became one of Brazil's first pedestrianised streets. Government buildings, old cinemas, markets and cheap lunch counters fill the grid. Rents in the older apartment blocks are among the lowest anywhere central, and every BRT line converges here.
bestFor: Budget travellers who want maximum transit access and the lowest central rents.
pros: Cheapest central apartments in the city
Every bus and BRT line passes through
Pedestrian streets, markets and museums on foot
cons: Empties out and feels unsafe after dark on weeknights
Older buildings with tired plumbing and lifts
Little greenery compared with the rest of Curitiba

name: Água Verde
tagline: Quiet mid-rise residential grid with parks and good schools
description: A settled family district just south of Batel, made of ten-storey blocks on calm tree-lined streets with bakeries, pharmacies and a good weekly market. Praça do Japão and Parque Barigui are both close by. It buys most of Batel's convenience for noticeably less money.
bestFor: Long-stay nomads and families who want quiet streets and value without leaving the centre-south.
pros: Better value per square metre than neighbouring Batel
Quiet streets, parks and everyday shops on foot
cons: Nightlife is minimal, you go to Batel for it
Few cafes set up for laptop work

name: Bigorrilho and Champagnat
tagline: Tower living on the edge of Parque Barigui
description: A vertical neighbourhood of newer high-rises spreading west from Batel towards the huge Parque Barigui. Runners and cyclists use the park daily. The mix is young professionals and students from nearby universities, with plenty of gyms, bakeries and delivery-friendly restaurants at street level.
bestFor: Nomads who want a new-build flat, a gym habit and a big park on the doorstep.
pros: Newest apartment stock with good internet and amenities
Parque Barigui running and cycling loops nearby
Quieter than Batel but a short walk from it
cons: Steep hills make some walks harder than they look
Main avenues clog badly at rush hour
Rents are climbing towards Batel levels

name: Rebouças
tagline: Converted brick warehouses, universities and a young crowd
description: An old industrial district by the rail line where red-brick factories have become universities, offices and event spaces such as the Shopping Estação complex. Student housing and small studios keep rents low, and a scattering of craft beer bars and coffee roasters has followed the young population in.
bestFor: Younger or budget-focused nomads who want cheap rent close to the centre and a student social scene.
pros: Low rents for how central it is
Walking distance to Centro and the bus terminal
Growing craft beer, coffee and events scene
cons: Gritty in patches, keep your bag close at night
Rail and truck noise on some streets
Very few parks or green streets
